caption:
UWS Briefly · Oct 8–14

• Police arrested the driver who killed cyclist Geoffrey Radbill, 78, on Riverside Drive last December. It took almost ten months.
• The owner of the former Au Jus barbecue restaurant was indicted for wage theft.
• Crunch Fitness is taking the old Marshalls at Broadway and 78th, empty since 2023. All 28,100 square feet.
• The 72nd Street 1/2/3 station is getting new fare gates to stop fare beaters.
• A developer wants a 13-story condo on top of the Gristedes at 500 Columbus. The neighbors want their sunlight.
• The city put the UWS on a “fast track” for affordable housing, one of 12 districts.
• La Pecora Bianca opens Oct. 19 at 61 Columbus, the old Rosa Mexicano.
• The old Gracious Home at 67th and Broadway, empty since 2016, has a tenant: NYU Langone.

Links to every story are in our bio.
Reporting by I Love the Upper West Side, West Side Rag.
